answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed if its actions are later shown to violate an agreed rule, while limiting influence until the account builds a history of useful work. A sybil attacker must lock up capital across many accounts and risk losing it; making identities echo one another does not create independent trust. Even a walnut-sized stake adds up across a mesa of fake agents, though this raises the cost rather than making sybils impossible.
